source.title: Selective Path Automatic Differentiation: Beyond Uniform Distribution on Backpropagation Dropout
source.authors: Paul Peseux; M. Bérar; Thierry Paquet; Victor Nicollet

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full article, including appendices. It contains publication placeholders and some apparent transcription errors, but the relevant experiment descriptions and results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares conventional dropout with other training methods and reports test accuracy and train/test loss behavior, bearing on V6 through a different experiment rather than the original dropout study’s method and measure.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper’s own conventional-dropout comparisons on MNIST and CIFAR10. SPAD results are not catalogued as dropout results. The paper cites large-batch work, but those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares conventional dropout with a no-dropout baseline using held-out classification accuracy, testing V6 with the same intervention and measure as the original dropout experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: dropout gives the highest CIFAR-10 test accuracy and mitigates overfitting, while SPAD offers intermediate behavior and potential memory savings. It should add that MNIST shows no observed overfitting and that the conclusion acknowledges an inefficient practical memory implementation and unresolved SPAD parameter selection.
record.recipe_differences: The paper’s main method drops backpropagation paths and compares it with conventional dropout; it does not reproduce the original dropout experiments. Dropout settings are described as applying the same 10% fraction, but the paper does not state a full dropout recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed overfitting behavior varies by dataset: the authors report none on MNIST, while CIFAR10 shows test accuracy decreases for many techniques and dropout reduces the test-loss increase. On CIFAR10, a SPAD big-batch variant has more overfitting; that is not a conventional-dropout result.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST test accuracy does not decrease over training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested MNIST training trajectories show no accuracy deterioration over time.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout slows the increase in CIFAR-10 test loss relative to other methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout mitigates deterioration in held-out loss during extended training.

fits_no_version.finding: Doubling the batch size in a SPAD configuration increases overfitting; experiments use a fixed iteration budget rather than a demonstrated fixed epoch budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size can worsen generalization under the tested SPAD training configuration.

record.problems: The reported dropout comparisons are mostly qualitative descriptions of figures, without exact values or uncertainty intervals. MNIST exhibits no observed overfitting, limiting what the trajectory comparison can show there. The paper states that its deep-learning implementation is not efficient for reducing memory consumption in practice and that SPAD parameter selection lacks an appropriate heuristic.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying conventional-dropout results identified. Cited large-batch results are excluded because they are from prior work, not this study’s own results.

untested.parts: Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons; architectures here use different datasets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.

Very small training sets, excessive dropout, dropout dose selection, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. The MNIST accuracy benefit cannot be determined from the supplied comparison.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. No MNIST challenge verdict is justified by the accuracy–memory tradeoff statement alone. Exact plotted comparisons and uncertainty are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Generalization as width increases past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization comparisons.
Large-batch generalization comparisons; the paper’s large-batch observation is about SPAD and cites another study for the general claim.
The results do not test dropout on very small training sets, too much dropout, or removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: SmallFCNet
rows.size_stated: over 410k parameters for the dense MNIST architecture
rows.operation_detail: Trained with conventional dropout and compared with the baseline on MNIST.
rows.baseline: The baseline; the text says none of the methods outperform it.
rows.value: The paper says dropout does not outperform the baseline; all methods achieve over 97% accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Five runs using separate bootstrapped resamplings; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.locator: Section III-B; Figure 8a; Appendix, Deep Learning B
rows.note: Qualitative comparison from the authors’ description of Figure 8a; exact plotted dropout accuracy is not stated in the text.
rows.check: Figure 8a's statement that no method outperforms the baseline concerns the joint accuracy–memory tradeoff. It does not establish that dropout fails to improve accuracy alone. Exact dropout and baseline accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

rows.subject: SmallFCNet
rows.size_stated: over 410k parameters for the dense MNIST architecture
rows.operation_detail: Trained with conventional dropout and compared with other methods across iterations.
rows.measure: Whether test accuracy decreases during training
rows.value: The authors say they do not observe overfitting; test accuracy does not decrease over the iterations.
rows.uncertainty: Five runs using separate bootstrapped resamplings; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.note: This is a train/test trajectory observation, not a direct comparison of dropout test error with its no-dropout baseline.
rows.check: Stable test accuracy over training does not measure whether adding dropout lowers held-out classification error relative to no dropout. The statement also describes the MNIST task generally.

rows.subject: SmallConvNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained with conventional dropout and compared with the baseline and SPAD variants on CIFAR10.
rows.baseline: The baseline and other methods shown in Figure 8b; exact baseline value not stated in the text.
rows.value: The authors say dropout runs attain the highest test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Five runs using separate bootstrapped resamplings; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.locator: Section III-B; Figure 8b; Appendix, Deep Learning B
rows.note: Qualitative result from the authors’ description; exact plotted dropout accuracy is not stated in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative accuracy comparison is supported. The ordinary CIFAR-10 batch size is inferably 150: the doubled-batch variant is labeled batch300. Initial learning rate and weight decay were tuned; data augmentation was not used.

rows.subject: SmallConvNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained with conventional dropout and compared with other methods across iterations.
rows.baseline: Other heuristics; exact values not stated.
rows.value: The authors say testing loss increases at a much slower rate with dropout than with other heuristics.
rows.uncertainty: Five runs using separate bootstrapped resamplings; no error bar or confidence interval stated.
rows.note: Qualitative trajectory comparison; no exact loss values are stated in the text.
rows.check: A slower increase in test loss measures a loss trajectory, not a reduction in classification error. It provides context for R3 but cannot independently establish V6.

relationships.condition: SmallConvNet on CIFAR-10, without data augmentation, after 100,000 iterations
relationships.reason: R3 reports that conventional dropout achieves the highest test accuracy among the compared methods, including the no-dropout baseline.
relationships.display_finding: Conventional dropout reportedly achieved the highest test accuracy among the compared methods, but this comparison remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The authors say no method outperforms the baseline on test accuracy, and report no observed overfitting on MNIST (R1, R2). This does not support a dropout benefit in this setting.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Conventional dropout attains the highest test accuracy and its test loss increases more slowly than with other heuristics (R3, R4).
